title: Pattern Headings: Animals
summary: Pattern-heading list for animals. Subdivisions on the list are free-floating under headings for individual animals and groups of animals at all taxonomic levels (common or scientific names, wild or domestic, extinct and fossil animals, breeds, age and sex groups). Pattern headings are Fishes (animals in general) and Cattle (domestic animals). Excluded: Animals; Domestic animals; Livestock; individually named animals; [animal] as laboratory animals / as pets phrase headings; individual microorganisms. Form subdivisions remain valid LCSH but are not used by LC catalogers (LCGFT instead).
validation_rules: Subdivisions on this list are free-floating only under headings for individual animals and groups of animals at all taxonomic levels, whether established under common or scientific names, wild or domestic, including extinct and fossil animals (e.g. *Aedes aegypti*; *Aquarium fishes*; *Dinosaurs*; *Echinodermata, Fossil*; *Pets*; *Sheep*). (H 1147 sec. B)
The pattern also covers individual breeds or groups of domestic animals (e.g. *Tennessee walking horse*; *Poodles*) and age and sex groups (e.g. *Chicks*; *Foals*; *Cows*). (H 1147 sec. B)
Do not use subdivisions from this list free-floating under the general headings *Animals*, *Domestic animals*, or *Livestock*. (H 1147 sec. C)
Do not use subdivisions from this list under individually named animals such as *Seattle Slew (Race horse)* or *Morris (Cat)*. (H 1147 sec. C)

Do not use subdivisions from this list under phrase headings of the type *[animal] as laboratory animals* or *[animal] as pets*; instead assign the phrase heading together with a heading of the type *[animal]--[subdivision]*. (H 1147 sec. C)
Subdivisions from this list are not free-floating under headings for individual microorganisms; such combinations must be established editorially. (H 1147 sec. C)

A listed subdivision may be used free-floating under any heading in the category if appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file; an established variant phrase or subdivision in the authority file takes precedence. (H 1147 sec. D)
Only subdivisions marked 'May Subd Geog' (Yes) may be followed by a geographic subdivision ($z); e.g. `--Diseases--Treatment` may be subdivided geographically, `--Anatomy` may not. (H 1147 sec. E)

Subdivisions representing specific pathological conditions (`--Abnormalities`, `--Fractures`, `--Infections`, `--Virus diseases`, `--Wounds and injuries`) may be further subdivided by the subdivisions listed under `--Diseases` (e.g. `--Infections--Diagnosis`; `--Fractures--Treatment`). (H 1147 sec. E)
`--Parasites` and `--Surgery--Complications` may be further subdivided by subdivisions used under diseases. (H 1147 sec. E)

`--Dormancy`, `--Effect of altitude on`, `--Effect of fishing on`, `--Flight`, `--Flight--Physiological aspects`, `--Fluorescence`, `--Metamorphosis` (and its subdivisions), `--Vocalization`, and `--Vocalization--Regulation` are not established under *Fishes*; use them under other animals as appropriate. (H 1147 sec. E)
Do not use `--Toxicology` or `--Venom` under *Fishes*; they are established instead under *Poisonous fishes*. (H 1147 sec. E)
Do not use `--Handling` under *Fishes*; use the heading *Fish handling* instead. (H 1147 sec. E)
Do not use `--Marking` under *Fishes*; use the heading *Fish tagging* instead. (H 1147 sec. E)
`--Nests` is used only under individual nesting animals and groups of nesting animals. (H 1147 sec. E)
`--Breeding` = controlled mating/selection by humans; `--Reproduction` = the physiological process. (H 1147 sec. E)
`--Feeding and feeds` = nutritional preparations provided by humans; `--Food` = substances animals find or provide for themselves and their food habits. (H 1147 sec. E)
`--Housing` = shelters built by humans; `--Habitations` = natural shelters animals build (burrows, dens, lairs, lodges); `--Nests` under nesting animals. (H 1147 sec. E)
`--Psychology` = mental processes of animals; `--Psychological aspects` = influence of animals on the human mental condition. (H 1147 sec. E)

`--Religious aspects` may be further subdivided by individual religion or Christian denomination, but each heading *[animal]--Religious aspects--[religion or denomination]* must be established editorially (not free-floating); see H 1998. (H 1147 sec. E)
`--Colonization` may be further subdivided geographically to designate where the colony is being established. (H 1147 sec. E)

When using `--Effect of chemicals on`, `--Effect of drugs on`, `--Effect of insecticides on`, or `--Effect of pesticides on`, assign additional headings of the type *[individual chemical]--Physiological effect* for individual chemicals. (H 1147 sec. E)

Legal subdivisions on this list (`--Law and legislation`, `--Collection and preservation--Law and legislation`, `--Conservation--Law and legislation`, `--Control--Law and legislation`, `--Marketing--Law and legislation`) may be further subdivided by the subdivisions for legal topics in H 1154.5. (H 1147 sec. E)
`--Nomenclature (Popular)--French, [Italian, etc.]` takes the name of a language in place of the bracketed examples. (H 1147 sec. E)

Form subdivisions on this list are valid LCSH: `--Biography`, `--Catalogs and collections` (May Subd Geog), `--Classification`, `--Feeding and feeds--Recipes`, `--Housing--Specifications` (May Subd Geog), `--Identification`, `--Nomenclature`, `--Nomenclature (Popular)`, `--Nomenclature (Popular)--French, [Italian, etc.]`, `--Parasites--Identification`, `--Pedigrees`, `--Performance records`. (H 1147 sec. F)

`--Feeding and feeds--Recipes`, `--Housing--Specifications`, and `--Parasites--Identification` are used as form subdivision combinations under individual animals and groups of animals. (H 1147 sec. F)
[LC practice] LC catalogers no longer use form subdivisions ($v); they assign LCGFT terms instead. Form subdivisions remain available to other institutions per local policy. (H 1147 sec. F)

[LC practice] If an exceptional variant form is retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating subdivision form (H 195); otherwise propose changing the variant form (H 193). (H 1147 sec. D)

sections.heading: A. Recent revisions
sections.text: 2026-05: Updated template. Separated general and form subdivisions. Added instructions related to LCGFT implementation. Added new subdivisions.

sections.heading: B. Types of headings covered by the pattern
sections.text:
The headings covered by this pattern include headings for individual animals and groups of animals at all taxonomic levels, established using either common or scientific names, including animals in their natural or wild state, and those raised or cared for by humans. The pattern also covers headings for extinct and fossil animals.

Examples:

```
Aedes aegypti
Aquarium fishes
Bigeye tuna
Canada goose
Dinosaurs
Diptera
Dodo
Echinodermata, Fossil
Honeybee
Laboratory animals
Marine animals
Mollusks
Pets
Predatory animals
Sheep
```

Included are individual breeds or groups of domestic animals, for example, *Tennessee walking horse*; *Poodles*; and headings for age and sex groups, for example, *Chicks*; *Foals*; *Cows*.

sections.heading: C. Types of headings not covered
sections.text:
The general headings *Animals*; *Domestic animals*; and *Livestock* are excluded from this category. The category also does not include individually named animals such as *Seattle Slew (Race horse)* or *Morris (Cat)*.

The subdivisions below are also not used under phrase headings of the type *[animal] as laboratory animals* or *[animal] as pets*. Instead, these phrase headings are assigned along with headings of the type *[animal]--[appropriate subdivision from the list below]*.

Also excluded are headings for individual microorganisms. If a subdivision from this list is needed for use under a heading for an individual microorganism, it is established editorially rather than assigned as a free-floating subdivision.

sections.heading: D. General rule
sections.text:
The category is represented by two pattern headings: *Fishes* and *Cattle*. Establish subdivisions appropriate for animals in general under *Fishes*; establish subdivisions specific to domestic animals under *Cattle*. Subdivisions having restricted use or needing explanation are explained in notes.

Note: In August 1993, the pattern heading list for domestic animals, H 1148, was discontinued. The subdivisions on that list were integrated into this list, and the scope of coverage of this list was expanded to include domestic animals.

Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file.

Subject authority records may exist for headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on this list.

LC practice: If an exceptional variant form is to be retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating subdivision form following the procedures in H 195 if the reference does not yet exist. Otherwise, submit a proposal to change the variant form along with all bibliographic records requiring correction following the procedures in H 193.

sections.heading: F. List of form subdivisions
sections.text:
LC practice: As stated in H 1075, Library of Congress catalogers will no longer use form subdivisions. Instead assign an appropriate term or terms from Library of Congress Genre/Form Terms (LCGFT) to bring out the form(s) and/or genre(s) of the resource being cataloged. The form subdivisions maintained on this list are not available for use by LC catalogers. Catalogers at institutions external to LC may use them as dictated by their own institutional policies.

| Subdivision | May Subd Geog | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `$v Biography` |  | Use under types of animals for works of collective or individual biography. |
| `$v Catalogs and collections` | Yes | Use under types of natural objects for catalogs or collections of those objects. |
| `$v Classification` |  | Use under topical headings for works that consist of a systematic breakdown of a subject into its constituent categories or subtopics. |
| `$x Feeding and feeds $v Recipes` |  | Use this subdivision combination as a form subdivision under individual animals and groups of animals. |
| `$x Housing $v Specifications` | Yes | Use *--Housing* for the shelters and structures that humans construct and provide for wild or domestic animals. For the natural shelters and homes that animals build for themselves, use the subdivision *--Habitations*. Use this subdivision combination as a form subdivision under individual animals and groups of animals. |
| `$v Identification` |  | Use for works presenting the characteristics of a group for the purpose of determining the names of its members. |
| `$v Nomenclature` |  | Use *--Nomenclature* for systematically derived lists of names or designations that have been formally adopted or sanctioned, or for discussions of the principles involved in the creation or application of those names to taxonomic groupings of animals. |
| `$v Nomenclature (Popular)` |  | Use *--Nomenclature (Popular)* for lists or discussions of common names for animal groupings. |
| `$v Nomenclature (Popular) $x French, [Italian, etc.]` |  | Use *--Nomenclature (Popular)* for lists or discussions of common names for animal groupings. |
| `$x Parasites $v Identification` |  | Use this subdivision combination as a form subdivision under individual animals and groups of animals. |
| `$x Pedigrees` |  |  |
| `$x Performance records` |  |  |
